reason: 리뷰 거절: internal/app/finding_ops.go:106 `value == previous` compares two `any` values. Go panics ("comparing uncomparable type") when both sides hold the same uncomparable dynamic type, which is exactly what a finding whose stored `data->>'assignee'` is a JSON object or array produces: `saveDomain` (domain.go:338-342) passes the merged data plus `cloneMap(oldData)`, so a PUT that does not touch the field arrives with `map[string]any` on both sides. Reproduced directly against the new helper and against `(&App{}).validateResource(..., update=true)`: `runtime error: comparing uncomparable type map[string]interface {}` and `[]interface {}`. server.go:239 recovers it into a 500, so every later edit of that row (title, status, due_date) now fails where it returned 200 before this commit. Such rows are creatable on main: domain.go:279 type-checks only name/title/description/evidence/remediation, and the findings branch never read `assignee`, so any findings:write client could POST `{"assignee":{...}}`. Fix: compare the string forms (`prev, pok := previous.(string); s, sok := value.(string); pok && sok && prev == s`) or guard the comparison with a comparability check. / internal/app/finding_ops.go:96-99 the comment claims a legacy value is "skipped here rather than turning every later edit of that row into a 400", and the implementation note claims such rows are "'변경'으로 보고 거절된다". For object/array values the actual outcome is neither: a 500 panic. This is precisely the case the implementer flagged as unverified, so description and behavior diverge in the riskiest spot. / internal/app/openapi.json FindingUpdate.properties.assignee is still `{"type":"string"}` while the sibling FindingBulkPatch.properties.assignee already documents the exact rule this commit now enforces on POST /api/findings and PUT /api/findings/{id} (maxLength 200, x-max-bytes 200, 제어문자 금지, 양끝 공백 제거, 빈 문자열이면 해제). AGENTS.md §1 makes openapi.json part of the API contract; as merged, a client cannot predict the new 400.
